pages.text: Build a bloomery out of clay, load it with iron ore and charcoal, light it with a torch and wait. Only charcoal: the sulfur in coal ruins iron. What comes out is not an ingot but a bloom, a spongy lump of iron and slag that never melted. Siderite goes in roasted.
pages.title: The bloomery

pages.text: Overcharge it, two charcoal to every ore, and it runs hot: the iron soaks up carbon until it melts, and what is tapped is pig iron, run into a sand bed and set as pigs of cast iron.

Medieval smelters made it by accident and threw it away until they learned to use it; at Lapphyttan in Sweden a bloomery grown tall became Europe's first blast furnace. Cast iron builds the blast furnace, and the blast furnace makes pig iron by the tank.
